subject: Logic
title: Galileo's Paradox
description: A quick win: understand Galileo's Paradox.

hook.text: There are fewer perfect squares than natural numbers. Yet you can pair every number with its square.

buildup.text: 1→1, 2→4, 3→9, 4→16... every natural number maps to exactly one perfect square. None left over.

discovery.text: Galileo noticed this in 1638: an infinite subset can be the same "size" as the full set.

twist.text: This violates common sense—a part equals the whole? Only when both are infinite.

climax.text: Cantor later proved that some infinities are genuinely bigger than others. Not all infinities are equal.

punchline.text: Infinity: where the part equals the whole.

quiz.question: What did Galileo observe about natural numbers and perfect squares?
